pairs.distinction: Not being heard is about my voice being ignored by any official; local control is about where decisions get made, even by people who might listen.
pairs.reason: Someone ignored by their own city council and someone whose town is run from the state capital name different problems and would each pick one easily.

pairs.distinction: Freedoms is my own choices being taken away; democracy slipping is the shared system of courts, elections and press weakening.
pairs.reason: People who feel personally restricted and people worried about the system as a whole often aren't the same people, so both need a place to say it.

pairs.distinction: Accountability is leaders breaking promises and facing nothing; corruption is the rules bending for people with money.
pairs.reason: A broken campaign promise and a rich donor getting special treatment are different complaints, and the lines already say which is which.

pairs.distinction: Taxes is about what I pay and what I get for it; accountability is about leaders getting away with broken promises.
pairs.reason: Paying more for worse services is a money complaint that someone could have even with honest leaders, so the two don't blur.

pairs.distinction: Accountability is individual leaders facing no consequences; democracy slipping is the institutions themselves being worn down.
pairs.reason: One is about people in power and the other about the system that should hold them, and the reworded democracy line makes that clearer.

pairs.distinction: Not being heard is my own voice ignored today; democracy slipping is the system that guarantees that voice weakening over time.
pairs.reason: Feeling ignored by officials is common even where democracy is stable, so a person can easily tell which of the two they mean.

pairs.distinction: Infrastructure is the roads, water and power I depend on breaking down; taxes is the sense of paying more for less across the board.
pairs.reason: Crumbling roads are a concrete daily problem whether or not someone thinks about taxes, and a person can choose between them without thinking twice.

pairs.distinction: Infrastructure is things that exist but keep breaking; car-or-nothing is having no way to get around except driving.
pairs.reason: Potholes and water main breaks are a different problem from having no bus or sidewalk at all, so they belong in separate pains and groups.

pairs.distinction: Voting is about the choice in front of me at election time; misinformation is not trusting what I read about anything.
pairs.reason: Someone can trust the news and still not know which candidate fits them, so the two pains name different moments.
